texts.preamble: Rajesh Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 October, 2020 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh 1 Mcrc 37350/2020 Rajesh Sharma vs. State of Mp Gwalior, Dated :05/10/2020 Shri Anand Purohit, counsel for the applicant. Shri Cp Singh, Panel Lawyer for the respondent/ State.
texts.facts: Case diary is available. This first application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for grant of bail. The applicant has been arrested on 03/09/2020 in connection with Crime No.64/2020 registered at Police Station Phoop, Bhind for offence under Sections 420, 272, 273 read with Section 34 of IPC.
texts.arguments: It is submitted by the counsel for the applicant that according to the prosecution case, 200 liters of milk and 45 kilograms of Dalda ghee was seized from the Milk dairy and offence has been registered under an apprehension that the same may be adulterated, however, there is no report by Food Analyst to prima facie make out an offence under Section 420 of IPC. The applicant is in custody since 03/09/2020 and the trial is likely to take sufficiently long time and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution case. It is further submitted that neither any offence has been registered under Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 nor any penalty has been imposed. Per contra, it is submitted by the counsel for the State that since the Inspection Team had an apprehension that the applicant is involved Rajesh Sharma vs. State of MP in sale of adulterated edible foods articles, therefore, offences under Sections 420, 272, 273 of IPC have been registered. It is further submitted that according to the case diary, no offence under Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 has been registered. In reply, it is submitted by the counsel for the applicant that the offences under Sections 272, 273 of IPC are punishable up-to the rigorous imprisonment of six months' with fine of Rs.1,000/- and they are bailable. The Supreme Court has observed as under : "The issue of overcrowding of prisons is a matter of serious concern particularly in the present context of the pandemic of Corona Virus (COVID - 19). We direct that each State/Union Territory shall constitute a High Powered Committee comprising of (i) Chairman of the State Legal Services Committee, (ii) the Principal Secretary Rajesh Sharma vs. State of MP (Home/Prison) by whatever designation is known as, (ii) Director General of Prison(s), to determine which class of prisoners can be released on parole or an interim bail for such period as may be thought appropriate. For instance, the State/Union Territory could consider the release of prisoners who have been convicted or are undertrial for offences for which prescribed punishment is up to 7 years or less, with or without fine and the prisoner has been convicted for a lesser number of years than the maximum. The Supreme Court in the case of IN RE : CONTAGION OF COVID 19 VIRUS IN PRISONS by order dated 7-4-2020 has directed as under :- ''In these circumstances, we consider it appropriate to direct that Union of India shall ensure that all the prisoners having been released by the States/Union Territories are not left stranded and they are provided transportation to reach their homes or given Rajesh Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149479430/ 2 the option to stay in temporary shelter homes for the period of lockdown.
